Superb game. It took me a while to get used to the controls (i am not a controller person, and on keyboard you need to have really nimble fingers on this one, specially the stun-execute combo while moving) but once it did it, it went smooth till the end.

It's a simple game very well executed and with the full W40k flair. I am not supremely fond of the health system, but it mirror the inhuman qualities of the Legiones Astartes. Could have a bit more variety of enemies, but at the same time even if not much varied in type, they still do their job perfectly. 

Love the bullet time, and fury feels satisfactory and rewarding to unleash. I had a blast with this game, once again, I really really liked it. 83/100 on my personal charts (and mind, i rarely play and/or like action games)

For the Emperor, for Guilliman!

Space Marine is good for a 2006 3D action game.
Came out on 2011 ? o__O

- Graphics are ok. If you forgive the graphical bugs in landscape.
- Music is lazy and repetitive. I've found myself thinking "they could have done better, while playing".
- Gameplay is ok. But lacks of complexity... two options : Attack ranged, Attack weapons. This is too thin for 2011.
- RPG elements : none. The game is a hallway you run in.
- Difficulty : Rather challenging, if you forgive the battle you win with luck because the ennemies forgot to use their grenades. If they do you have no cover left and die like a little sack of ♥♥♥♥.
- Weapons are exceptionnal ! Exceptionnally bad since with almost any you need two shots to take out any serious ennemy. So you try to rush to contact because only in close combat can you regen your health. But in close combat you get flanked and killed like a little sack of ♥♥♥♥. So you play the coward hero cover and shoot until the coast is clear enough to regen some health on remaining ennemies. Some of the last "most powerful" weapon you get are the worst. Stick to the plasma rifle with charged shoot. It does the job.
- As usual you do the maintenance job ; of a giant mech this time : Open the doors, open the clampers, finish the polishing, get grease for the cogs, wash, clean etc. no seriously. I don't want to make a maintenance job when I play a game (you don't do only a giant mech, you also do other fun stuff but I'm not going to spoil it).
- Ennemies : I didn't knew orks were so good at ranged fights. Damn. And oh, you will fight orks, a lot. And chaos space marines... and that's it.
- Places : Raw buildings and desert. An raw buildings again. And again. And... again. I hope you like repetition.
- Story : Unfinished. And it surprises you sometimes. Like at the end. The game is over, yeah ! Good surprise ! No, seriously, you see everything coming a mile away. The end boss is not very satisfying and the middle boss is not either. Well, to get back to the story : you don't know the end of it.
- Space Marines : It's a good dive in the life of space marines, honor, heresy, trust and hard xenos ass-kicking.

So, so.

Don't play it. There are much better games that are out and do better. But if you are looking for a initiation to the WH40K Space Marine life it's a very good document... It would be better to take a book but pictures don't move in books.

Back when Space Marine came out, I thought it was the best 40k action game on the market. Replaying it now, I still do - but this time, it's because I know there isn't a good one.

Space Marine is many things - it's got that 40k feel both in looks and worldbuilding (keep in mind it was still made in the "No, you may not use our license for video games" era of Games Workshop), it's epic, but above all else, I now realize it's a horribly schizophrenical. The devs started with a cover shooter, but wanted something that incentivizes going in to kill enemies rather than hiding, and what they got was.... well. A bad cover shooter that tries to be a spectacle fighter and fails.

Sure, you recover health by executing enemies. That's... not nearly enough to make a good spectacle fighter. Especially not when you keep so many staples of the cover shooter genre (enemies with very strong hitscan attacks or aoes meant to push you out of cover) without the tools that genre gives you to survive (ability to stay in or quickly change cover). Instead, you have a melee system that's admittedly satisfying but also uninspired (one button for attack chain, one for stuns/finishers) and horribly, horribly weak - in fact, the best - the ONLY safe way to fight stronger melee-based enemies is to back away from them and shoot them in the face. Thinking of doing the reverse? HA forget it, the ranged enemies will gun you down as you try to approach (if you're lucky and even CAN approach them, what with gaps and unvaultable tiny walls), and even if you get in a scrap, the slow-ass executions will have you gunned down by every other enemy as you try to heal off one. It doesn't help that later stages of the game force you to pick whether you want to be all but useless at melee or at shooting, with limited options of changing between the two. Add in enemies piling on you with very limited CC on your side but they happily stunlock you for their followup attacks and all the gunfire coming your way, and you get a game that wasn't meant to be a cover shooter but is best played by finding a tiny nook or wall and praying that your armor can recharge.

And the worst part? The WORST part? It's STILL the best 40k action game out there. Gah.

Multiplayer is great, or at least was back then, no idea if it's still played.

I have mixed feelings about this game.
Firstly, with the Warhammer stamp on it then it's an awesome game. great feeling to it with your playing as a really tough space marine mowing down orks in your path and seeing them being obliterated in front of you. Great selection of guns that relate to the game and give you a good understanding of how awesome and powerful it is to wield these power houses.
Fun game if you know a lot about Warhammer and like Warhammer.

Secondly without the warhammer stamp on it, I feel as though the gameplay is lacking.. these is no real decisions you have to make with what weapons you have to take in and battleground awareness isn't really needed either as there is always a drop right in front of the checkpoint with all the guns in the game.
This means that it is really a mash the button and not be swamed game. They spent a lot of time with the graphics but lacked in everything else.
The only good gameplay where is felt like you were a part of it was at the end boss cinematic. That's it.
